findings.title: Definitive local refusal leaves an uneditable pending payload
findings.trigger: Enter provider_id as whitespace, valid model and loopback base URL, then save. HTML required permits whitespace, trim yields empty provider_id and the actual source-bound validator returns INVALID_REQUEST_SCHEMA before any host.configure HTTP request.
findings.observed: pendingPayload was set before the call and is cleared only for protocol REJECTED or successful unwrap. Local refusal has neither; all inputs stay disabled and Continue Same Configuration repeatedly submits the unfixable bytes. Independent DOM test confirms zero configure HTTP requests and repeated refusal.
findings.impact: A recoverable local input mistake prevents correcting/saving configuration. The existing shell also retains a write operation created before definitive request validation, so clearing only the UI ref is insufficient for this branch.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish definitely-not-dispatched refusal from uncertain/acknowledged commands. Validate normalized inputs before setting pending, and ensure known pre-dispatch rejection releases the corresponding shell operation while retaining all uncertain/ACK lifetimes. Preserve visible input for correction.

findings.title: Pending configuration cannot be recovered after route unmount
findings.trigger: Receive ACKNOWLEDGED for configuration, leave the settings/workbench route and return. Component-local pendingPayload and form are recreated empty while the shell retains the acknowledged operation.
findings.observed: Submitting another model then returns COMMAND_PENDING with no new configure HTTP call. The component stores and locks the new payload, so its Continue button can never replay the original pending command. Independent DOM test reproduces this with unmount/remount and actual IPC/validator.
findings.impact: Ordinary navigation loses the supported recovery path and can block subsequent write commands for the same desktop state. A user would have to reproduce the exact original payload outside the locked form or restart the shell; neither is provided as a safe UI recovery flow.
findings.suggestion: Expose/recover the pending public command identity and original payload from the shell across component lifetimes, or keep an equivalent durable UI command owner. Do not replace an existing pending operation with the payload rejected by COMMAND_PENDING; retain the original envelope and command_id until its terminal response.
